questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That there were English courses in my field. That it was evaluated well be former Erasmus students from my university, and that the academic help at the receiving institution had been evaluated really well. Also the nature & that it was a country I had never been to before.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Everything at the receiving institution was amazing and went super well. The only thing that could have been a lot better is the help I got from Copenhagen University. Sp therefore I advice everyone to start really early when getting pre-approvals early, since the university is not helping you and it takes ages to get answer on e-mails. I am sad to say that I almost didn't get my approval on time, even though I started in March. So just start early :-)

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The student desk at Haskoli Islands is there to answer everything, and most of it your don't even have to ask for, since they already give you the information on a pre-arrival meeting.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was very well organised and the information was good.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Honestly, I was lucky to know someone., Finding housing in Reykjavik on your own is very hard, and I have heard several stories of expats being scammed. So if you know someone who have been there, contact them and first and foremost sign up for on-campus housing. There are two sites, ask the university.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Reykjavik is really small and everything that happens in downtown or at University, therefore it can affect your stay a lot if you live "far" away fromt he center. And this can be just a few kilometers even, it will feel longer as soon as you get there, because Reykjavik is so small. If you have to catch a bus etc. to go to campus, this can be a social disadvantage, since many deals/social gatherings etc. may happen quite spontaneously. So sign up for on-campus housing early and remember to activate your application every month (don't forget it like I did). If you are not that lucky, find something close to downtown (postal code: 101) or in Vesturbajær and get a bike.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think the on-campus housing is really nice, however there is just not enough.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was so easy, you just fill in a form online. They send the information. And when you get there everything is already set up on their "Absalon" (it is called Ugla). If something is not working the student desk will help you.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The student/service desk everyday

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful. Just check and make sure that they are taught in the semester your are there.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just do what you are being told and don't stress about deadlines. They will inform you well

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I learned some interesting things and the professors were nice. However, I did not choose my exchange for the courses, so they were not my dream-courses

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They are quite strict, so I was REALLE LUCKY to be allowed to take a MA-course, don't expect this. The bachelor-courses were a bit easier than at KU, but you need to interact and engage in the teaching.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much more inclusive. They expect you to ask questions, have an opinion etc.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Small States Theory: Opportunities and Constraints of Small States in the International System
The Power Potential of Small States in the European Union
All that glitters is not gold: gender, equality and sustainability in Iceland
Term Paper in Small States Studies (online course)
Arctic Politics in International Context

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The Power Potential of Small States in the European Union & Arctic Politics in International Context
The others I didn't find particular interesting, but that is a matter of taste. I think having small states courses and/or Arctic courses is quite nice, since it is what Haskoli Islands is specialising in.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to rent cars to go on trips around. This cost something but prioritize it, it is wort it. Buy a bik to go around in Reykjavik or walk.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing is very expensive unless you are as lucky as I or get on-campus housing. The prices are not that different (higher) than DK, but still expect higher prices they are. But not insanely

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Cheap gym with yoga-classes etc. available

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Different events: Going to local pools, trips, community dining etc

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Just see what is available and go to somethings

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Rent a car and go on roadtrips with other exchange students. Go north, south, to the Westman Islands, the East etc. And take trips longer than two days also if you want. There is a four day hike Laugavegur, which I recommend especially.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Say yes to things your mentors invite you to

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Pools:-)))

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Like any other location: Be open & say yes to ideas, invitations etc. in the beginning and don't be shy to write in big exchange groups if people want to go swimming/to a bar/dancing/to the beach etc.
Use happy hours - most bars have happy hours, find a guide in Reykjavik Grapevine paper that can be found e.g. in the supermarket Kronan. Bónus is the cheapest supermarket! E.g. Prikið, Jungle Cocktail have good happy hours. The student cellar alway have "cheap" beer for students
By a 20-trip pass for the pools in Reykjavik, it is amazing. Nautholsvik by the beach is also amazing
Food: Napoli, Chickpea, Mandi, Nordic House 
Experiences: Bio paradis, Gaukerrin (karaoke every tuesday), Le Kock (jazz jam every monday evening)
Dowload Aurora map and see some Northern Lights in the fall/winter

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Contact Haskoli Islands if you have questions

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting international students

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing between studying and social acitivities. Remember you only have to pass your exams (the grades don't transfer) so choose social activities

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
